name: Scrolling Popups
description: Island-event popups get scrollbars when their text does not fit: a popup is never taller than the screen (its buttons stay at its bottom, where they always are), and when its text is taller than the room left, or has a line wider than the box (one very long word), a vertical and/or a horizontal scrollbar appears, drawn with the game's own scrollbar pictures. Scroll with the mouse wheel over the popup, the arrows, by dragging the knob or by clicking the bar; the text starts at the top and starts over when the result replaces the question. A popup whose text fits looks and works exactly as before. This first stage covers the island-event popups (and Custom Island Events from Story / Cheat Upgrades, which use them); the text a popup can hold is still the game's 2,000 characters. There is no keyboard scrolling. Nothing is saved, so the patch can be ticked or unticked at any time. **Needs no other patch.** Off by default; Owner's Defaults ticks it. **Unverified in play: the effect has not been tested live.** The companion is "VVFP Scrolling Popups.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; if it cannot be loaded, the popups are as the game draws them.
behavior_changes: The island-event dialog (constructor 0x4192F0): its `call 0x40DDD0` sizing the panel (0x41983F) calls VVFP Scrolling Popups.dll, which caps the height to the screen's (600 px, read from the drawing context) less 16 px above and below; the game then centres the panel and places its buttons from the bottom.

Its draw's `call 0x40A0C0` drawing the body text (0x418591) calls the companion, which measures the text with that same routine (measure only) and its words with the game's counted draw; when the text fits the box (the panel's bottom less the room the dialog keeps for its buttons: 4 x a choice button's height with two choices, else 5/2 x the OK button's) it makes the stock call unchanged; otherwise it sets the drawing context's clip rectangle (+0x60) to the box, draws the text moved by the scroll position, restores the clip, and draws the scrollbars with the game's own pictures (image ids 0x1B-0x1E, 0x19, 0x1A: Up/DownArrowButton, VerticalScrollTrack tiled, VerticalScrollKnob, WideSlider2, sliderhandle).

The event pump's `call 0x4020A0` handing a mouse event to the game (0x40451E) calls the companion first: a press on a scrollbar of the dialog drawn this moment, a knob drag and its release are used by the companion and not passed on; every other event goes to the game unchanged. The wheel is read by an SDL event watch (SDL_AddEventWatch, SDL_MOUSEWHEEL).

A word wider than the text box (a long unbroken word) hangs the stock game: its justified paragraph backs off to an empty line and tries the same word again, for ever. The constructor's four measures of the dialog's texts (0x419611, 0x419648, 0x419681, 0x4197F7, `call 0x40A0C0`, measure only) call the companion, which gives the paragraph the width of the text's widest word when that is wider than the box (the words measured with the game's counted draw, cut where the paragraph cuts them); the draw wraps at that same width and the box scrolls sideways.
explicit_non_changes: No executable byte is patched: the companion writes the three sites at run time, only after verifying their stock bytes and the instructions before them (all of them, or none).
A popup whose text fits is drawn by the very same call as in the stock game; the dialog's text field keeps its 2,000-byte size; keys, the buttons, the events and the save are unchanged.
evidence_status: implemented from exact-build disassembly; the shipped companion emulated on the published executable's own dialog constructor and draw code with the game's own fonts and pictures (tests/test_scrolling_popups.py: the panel capped, the clip set and restored, wheel, arrows, knob drag and track clicks moving the drawn lines, the buttons at the panel's bottom, a fitting text drawn exactly as the stock game draws it); runtime/player confirmation pending
